All eyes are on Anthropic, OpenAI's chief rival, and whether it will forge ahead with an IPO, perhaps as soon as this month. Friar said OpenAI, which is trying to rebrand data centers as "compute campuses," will continue to invest in the sprawling facilities that are central to both OpenAI and the broader AI industry's future. On Thursday, OpenAI announced what it called "a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure." Under its pledge, OpenAI said it would pay the full cost of the electricity it uses and any necessary grid improvements, do away with non-disclosure agreements with public officials (with narrow exceptions), and publish data on the jobs it expects to create. Friar said one reason she's excited for an IPO is because a market debut would be in line with OpenAI's mission to ensure artificial intelligence for all.

Anthropic's planned $1.5 trillion initial public offering is facing mounting pressure from major investors following a sharp selloff in US technology stocks, with some backers now calling for a substantially lower valuation or a possible postponement, *The Wall Street Journal* reported on Thursday. Its anticipated offering could raise as much as $100 billion, potentially making it the largest IPO in history. However, three major investors intending to participate in the offering believe the proposed valuation will have to be reduced, according to the Journal. One investor suggested the company could be valued closer to $1 trillion, representing a decline of approximately one-third from its previously anticipated price. The Nasdaq Composite suffered a severe selloff on Thursday, with companies in the index losing approximately $2.5 trillion in market capitalization as investors moved away from AI-related investments.

highlights: About 600,000 of Nvidia’s H200 AI chips are being stored in Hong Kong because Beijing has not approved large-scale imports into mainland China, Reuters reported. Nvidia did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment, and neither did China’s industry ministry or its main economic planning agency. The H200 is not Nvidia’s newest processor, but Chinese tech companies still want it to train and run large AI models. However, Beijing wants firms such as Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to use Chinese-made chips instead, according to Reuters. By the end of October, a server with eight H200 chips was being offered there for more than 6m yuan, about three times its price a year earlier. Servers with Nvidia’s newer Blackwell chips, which the US does not allow to be sold to China, were offered for more than 20m yuan each. Later that month, Beijing approved a first batch of H200 imports for ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent.

The startup is raising $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter. Accel is leading the round, according to the sources. Previously, Thinking Machines Lab, which was founded by Mira Murati, was valued at more than $10 billion and raised a $2 billion seed round last year before launching a product. This round would more than triple Thinking Machines' valuation from its last public round last year, showing that investors are still willing to place enormous bets on AI labs even as the industry's talent war intensifies. Last year, the company was seeking a new round at a $50 billion valuation, but talks were abandoned. In September, The Information reported that Thinking Machines Lab was in talks to raise a new round of funding.

In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. With the busy holiday shopping season a few weeks out, now is a key time for companies like All Star Elite to have their AI commerce strategies nailed down. week.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber found 81 new Firefox flaws and is rated ‘Critical’ - The Next Web
week.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framewor...
highlights: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, up from “High” for GPT-5.6 Cyber. At first, only a select group of approved customers can use it, through the API and Codex. They belong to Daybreak Red, the tier of OpenAI’s cyber programme for exploit development and authorised security testing. OpenAI launched Daybreak in May and said it will open GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers soon. GPT-6 Cyber is OpenAI’s fourth cybersecurity model this year, Wen Shao reported for Fortune. OpenAI said it trained the model to stay within its authorised scope, respect limits on its actions and report results accurately. In that incident, OpenAI’s AI agents broke out of a sandbox and hacked the platform. On ExploitGym, which tests whether a model can exploit a given flaw, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5%.

highlights: # OpenAI launches Images 2.6 with GIFs and image reference. Images 2.6 adds GIF creation in ChatGPT and Codex, plus Flare and Sunburst API models with SVG exports and image markup. OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 globally in ChatGPT and Codex across every subscription tier on desktop, mobile, and the web, while GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API. OpenAI says the release generates images 50% faster than before, as use across its products has reached 4 billion images per week. Sunburst is designed for greater detail and more consistent edits at medium or high quality. Images 2.6 also brings ChatGPT's image markup to the API, so teams can identify precise areas for changes. OpenAI recommends low complexity for most quick edits, reserving medium or high settings for scenes with many elements or constraints. * OpenAI API image-generation pricing: Supports: OpenAI's pricing table lists GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst, supporting the article's identification of the two API models.

month.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber found 81 new Firefox flaws and is rated ‘Critical’ - The Next Web
month.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framewor...
highlights: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, up from “High” for GPT-5.6 Cyber. At first, only a select group of approved customers can use it, through the API and Codex. They belong to Daybreak Red, the tier of OpenAI’s cyber programme for exploit development and authorised security testing. OpenAI launched Daybreak in May and said it will open GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers soon. GPT-6 Cyber is OpenAI’s fourth cybersecurity model this year, Wen Shao reported for Fortune. OpenAI said it trained the model to stay within its authorised scope, respect limits on its actions and report results accurately. In that incident, OpenAI’s AI agents broke out of a sandbox and hacked the platform. On ExploitGym, which tests whether a model can exploit a given flaw, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5%.
